chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Rayyan ibn Shabib
Maridah left a will to a group of Christians who were servants, so we said: Distribute this among the poor Muslims from your companions.
So I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) and said to him: Indeed, my sister left a will to a group of Christians, and I wanted to divert that to a group of Muslims from our companions.
He said: 'Execute the will according to what she willed.'
Allah, the Exalted, said: 'Indeed, the sin is upon those who change it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a Muslim leaves a will to non-Muslims?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that a Muslim's bequest to non-Muslims remains valid and should not be redirected to Muslims, emphasizing the principle of honoring the testator's specific intent. He supports this ruling by citing the Quranic principle that the burden of altering a divine or legal decree falls upon the one who changes it, rather than the original decree itself. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the validity of the will is tied to the testator's will, provided the bequest is lawful, and deviation requires justification.
